Expiry (bronze, silver and gold each expire their own snapshots, with controls) unreferences files, and pyiceberg has nothing that deletes them (#3361), so the warehouse grew a file per table per sync for ever -- integrity.py measured it and check_mirror reported it. python -m scripts.remove_orphan_files is Iceberg's own remove_orphan_files for a local warehouse, with its two safeguards taken whole: only files older than a margin (72 h, Iceberg's three-day default -- a file a write has not yet committed is unreferenced too), and only files NO snapshot in the history references, so every retained snapshot and every published-N tag keeps its files. claim: an erasure (right-to-be-forgotten) workflow
status: BUILT TO THE OWNER'S THREE DECISIONS (2026-10-12). (1) EVERYWHERE, REWRITTEN: python -m scripts.erase Type id --reason ... --write records the keys, rewrites every mirror table holding them (bronze, silver, changelog, quarantine, gold, gold_history, gold_conflicts -- mapped from the ontology's own storages and links, so a person is the object AND everything linking to it), drops every older tag and snapshot, and deletes the files outright; tested by opening every Parquet file in the warehouse and finding the person in none while an untouched customer remains. (2) SUPPRESSED UNTIL THE SOURCE CATCHES UP: every sync drops their rows on the way in and reports how many erased keys a source still returns; the register records when it stops. (3) RE-APPLIED ON RESTORE: the register is backed up, a restore keeps the NEWER register (it only grows) and marks every erasure unpurged, and the server refuses to start until a sync has applied them. THE REGISTER HOLDS NO ID: salted hashes, the salt kept inside it so a restore brings both back. Cannot erase the SOURCE, which Elysium only reads; it says what the source still holds.

claim: value kinds and per-value enrichment provenance
status: SURVEYED IN FULL AND PARTLY BUILT, and the survey is the useful half: NO VALUE-KIND VOCABULARY EXISTS ANYWHERE. The complete set of field attributes the code reads is cardinality, column, constraints, data_type, decimal_places, on_violation, prefer, readable, required, standardise, status, storage, survivorship, target, timezone, type, via_*, visibility -- not one of them epistemic. `type` is structural (data or link), `data_type` is representational, and `status` is a SCHEMA lifecycle label (active/experimental/deprecated) that is defaulted in by visible_schema and declared in no fixture. Zero hits for `confidence` across core/, api/, templates/, ui/. AND THERE IS NOTHING TO ATTRIBUTE YET: no enrichment or derivation pipeline exists. standardise.py is the only thing that changes a value and is meaning-preserving by charter ('every rule declared, never inferred'); core/functions/ is agent tooling that persists nothing; reverse links are the only computed property and are computed from structure. Inference exists only for identity and only as proposals that a person approves. PER-VALUE PROVENANCE: one slice built. Everything the lake records about origin is per ROW -- `_silo`/`_source_table` name one source for a whole object, `_fused_from` names every contributing storage without saying which contributed what, and fusion.py says so in those words -- EXCEPT the gold_conflicts table, which is per field, per source, and had no reader: a repo-wide search found the writer, the namespace constant and two assertions in test_survivorship.py. survivorship.py's own docstring promised what it could not deliver -- 'deleting losing values destroys trust. A person asking why the golden record says Leeds needs to see that the CRM said Hull and was outranked' -- while the losers went to a table nobody could read, which is the bin with extra steps. Now readable: core/mirror/gold_conflicts.py, GET /objects/{type}/{id}/conflicts gated as /provenance is plus object visibility plus per-field read grants on the values, and a section on the object hub beside the lineage. AND IT FOUND TWO DEAD ROUTES ON THE WAY: /provenance and /published-history both looked for a `_catalog` attribute on one of the mediator's adapters, which GoldConnector does not have (it holds its catalog inside the reader it delegates to) -- and GOLD-9 made reads gold-only, so GoldConnector is the only adapter there is. Both have answered 'nothing recorded' on every real deployment since, and their tests passed because they guarded assertions with `if body is not None`. Fixed with a public `catalog` on both adapters and one helper, plus the assertion that was missing. PER-FIELD ATTRIBUTION BUILT 2026-10-12, as the owner chose: every fused gold row carries `_field_sources`, {field: source} for each non-null value, written by both fusion paths (the GOLD-5 join and GOLD-6 survivorship) -- the winner for every field, not only where sources disagreed. Served as `field_sources` on /provenance, MAC-checked and filtered to readable fields (the row's four opaque identifiers keep the ungated decision /conflicts records), and shown on the object hub as 'Which source supplied each value', with the silo relabelled 'Primary silo' on a fused object. The two R67 substitutions were closed by R67a/R67b. WHAT REMAINS FOR R38: the value-kind vocabulary (nothing to attribute until an enrichment pipeline exists) and per-property timestamps (declined in survivorship.py for want of one).

claim: an imputation policy (never into served data)
status: VERIFIED: NOTHING IMPUTES A DATA VALUE INTO SERVED OBJECT DATA. Swept every layer and read the code rather than the names. field_types.coerce returns None for None and RAISES on anything unparseable -- no default, no fallback-to-string, and it refuses NaN, infinity, over-precise decimals and timezone guessing rather than rounding. transform.py keeps the RAW value on a coercion failure and names the column in a drift report, with a comment saying why: substituting would destroy the evidence. The only value-changing rule in standardise.py is null_if, which goes the other way -- a DECLARED sentinel becomes null. gold.py and gold_arrow.py give a missing column a typed null (pa.nulls) and the audit then refuses the publication if the field is required. The mediator's read path has no .get with a non-None default on any field value; an ungranted or deleted field is None and an ungranted link is [] (uniform denial). No Pydantic response field turns an absent value into a concrete one. Aggregates EXCLUDE null group values and null field values before grouping, so sum([]) and avg([]) are structurally unreachable and no null is ever counted as zero. The UI's single renderer refuses the falsy bug explicitly -- zero and false are left alone, null renders as an em dash. No fillna or coalesce anywhere in the pipeline; the two repo-wide matches are SQL COALESCE over internal counters. BUT THE SWEEP FOUND THREE FABRICATED CLAIMS ONE LEVEL UP, all in the merge reviewer's surface and all FIXED. (1) _readable_fields looked up visible_schema()['object_types'], a key that function has never produced, so it returned the empty set for every caller since it was written; its one consumer fetches readable & agreement fields, both rows came back {}, and a reviewer was told 'one side missing' about every field of every proposal while the true verdict sat unread -- with `withheld` naming every field, so the masking looked as though it were working. (2) masked_review._verdict tested KEY presence, but get_object returns a key for every field it is ASKED for, so that verdict only ever meant 'not fetched' = 'unreadable' and never once meant what it says; it now tests the VALUE and is told readability explicitly, so withheld, genuinely-null and not-compared are three different answers (DEV_UI 9.7's rule). (3) matching.py read Splink's three-valued gamma as two: -1 means the pair could not be compared because a value was null, and bool(gamma > 0) folded that into 'differ' -- presenting a null as evidence against a match, to a human deciding whether two records are the same person. A feature with a typed client and no screen, so nobody would have seen any of it by looking. Three controls added. NOT FIXED, recorded as R67: survivorship fills a null from another source with no per-PROPERTY record of having done so, and the pending-write overlay supplies a value the source does not hold into reads, aggregates, charts and the CSV export with no marker on the read path.

status: DONE, with the decision the row asked for: the check runs ON READ, when a manage:deployment holder's client asks for its notifications -- the dead man's switch (Healthchecks.io, Cronitor), where the sync's check-ins are its sync_attempts rows. claim: --accept-deletions updates silver and leaves gold refusing. The flag reaches IcebergMirrorSync and nothing else; build_gold has no such parameter and its own 'more than 50% of the last publication is gone' guard is unconditional. So an operator who follows iceberg_sync.py's own remedy after a genuine mass deletion gets silver moved, gold refused, and every reader still on the pre-deletion rows -- reported, not silent, but with no documented next step. Pinned by test_a_source_changes_and_what_a_reader_sees.py::TestAChangeTheMirrorRefuses. NEEDS A DECISION before it can be built: the flag names silo.table and gold is keyed by OBJECT TYPE, one type can span several tables, so carrying the escape across means deciding what the operator names and whether one accepted table licenses publishing a type built from three. Two independent layers refusing is the design working; the gap is that only one of them has a door
status: DONE. The operator's --accept-deletions now reaches gold: run_sync.deletions_accepted_for decides per TYPE -- its guard yields when every table deciding which objects it HAS was accepted: the primary storage, and for an identity-resolved type every storage; an additional (joined) storage alone licenses nothing, since it cannot shrink the type. build_gold then skips only the more-than-half-gone check; every other audit still runs. The matrix test that pinned the gap now asserts the reader sees the deletion, with a control that gold still refuses without the flag; tests/unit/test_accept_deletions_reaches_gold.py proves run_sync passes it.
